tasks.behavior: Implement hosted and origin-restricted embedded checkout
acceptance: Hosted integration works without a browser package; full and element embeds reuse trusted checkout and support existing payment lifecycles.
Only configured exact origins can frame an embed; normal pay pages remain unframeable; loopback HTTP is test-only and live returns require HTTPS.
Message origin/source checks, strict CSP, revocation, expiration and forged parent/redirect events are tested; browser hints never prove fulfillment.

tasks.behavior: Build minimal JavaScript and React checkout packages
acceptance: Browser packages provide PayButton, Checkout and PaymentElement over existing checkout URLs, without secret keys or client-authoritative financial state.
Typed messages verify origin/source and mount lifecycle cleans listeners; React 18 and 19 compatibility, type/build/size and packed-install checks pass.
Release artifacts, changelogs and provenance CI are prepared; publishing remains gated by separate approval.

tasks.behavior: Prove merchant checkout fulfillment and reconciliation end to end
acceptance: The example merchant prices a cart on its server, creates real checkouts, verifies events and fulfills an order once across hosted and embedded flows.
Independent shared-link customers, client invoicing, multi-store isolation, expiration, partial payment, delivery recovery and spoofed prices/messages have automated workflow coverage.
Ledger/export totals reconcile against receiver and wallet chain balances; duplicate/reordered events cannot double-fulfill.
Quickstart and integration docs match implemented packages; provider limitations, actual user testing and release approvals are reported truthfully.

tasks.behavior: Recover payment processing and enforce revocation and webhook fairness
acceptance: Incomplete RPC logs never create permanent conflicts; previously affected deposits recover only after exact canonical evidence is verified.
Large verified deposit backlogs make bounded durable progress, preserve exact allocation and event semantics, and settle without duplicate booking. Invoice creation and expiry use one timestamp.
Role changes recheck current actor permissions under the profile lock, preventing pending requests from undoing a demotion.
Webhook test and resend work has bounded tenant budgets; slow tenants cannot occupy every sender slot or starve other profiles.
notes: 2026-10-28 review pass by independent-reviewer: No remaining findings. Reviewed canonical deposit recovery, append-only conflict resolutions, genuine contradiction gates, bounded ledger prefixes, historical paid proofs, refund tails, expiry and settlement reconciliation. Reviewed role checks under the profile lock, tenant scheduling, queue caps, lease deadlines and stale completion protection. Checked invoice transaction-clock consistency, structure and unchanged packages. Focused receiver and webhook race tests passed; final docs-check, unit, build, e2e and keep checks passed.

proof.1: unit: Missing-log retry and legacy-conflict recovery pass with exact canonical proof, immutable resolutions and genuine contradictions still blocking.
proof.2: unit: Bounded batches preserve exact balances, expiry funding, refund-tail reconciliation and once-only events. Delayed creation preserves the requested lifetime and invoice lines. A disposable 20000-deposit benchmark committed its first 100 in 153ms and drained exactly in 31.8s processing time.
proof.3: unit: A paused role-change request returns 403 after its actor is demoted and cannot restore Admin access.
proof.4: unit: Tenant and endpoint leases enforce concurrency caps across senders; late profiles progress during slow delivery, persistent backlogs rotate and concurrent manual enqueue respects capacity.
